Fix a calculation in a teammate's module (he is asleep; keep the change minimal, well-commented and tested; do NOT commit or push). Repo /Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/StartMunichHack/ask-soony. You may edit only src/ask_soony/verifier/impact/shortfall.py (and timing.py if needed), src/ask_soony/dispatch/decisions/cards.py only if a headline/text depends on the changed numbers, their tests under src/ask_soony/verifier/**/tests/ and src/ask_soony/dispatch/decisions/tests/, and write a short note for the teammate at /Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/StartMunichHack/ask-soony/src/ask_soony/verifier/NOTE_FOR_FARHAN.md (plain text, no em dashes).

Problem: `uv run python -m ask_soony.dispatch.decisions --root data/portal --out /tmp-like-path` (use /Users/jonasstenglein/.claude/jobs/3021cc1a/tmp/verifier-fix/dispatch.json as out; never write data/state) produces "Game Card 128 GB – Grand Heist 6: 34,800 short across 2 editions" = needed 153,200 - book stock 118,400 (stock snapshot as of 2026-11-20). It ignores supply that arrives BEFORE the end of packing: e.g. Hwaseong's 28,000 game cards (PO 4500318735, AWB 020-48113256, flown ICN-FRA, delivered to Hamburg this weekend per the shipping advice in suppliers/SUP-0010_Hwaseong_Memory/order_confirmations/Shipping_advice_020-48113256_4500318735.pdf and the open shipments / launch plan inbound rows) and any other inbound whose ETA is before the end of packing (Sun 20:00) or that already arrived after the stock snapshot. An independent check (src/ask_soony/papercheck.py rule a) computes ~6,800 short for this part when counting stock plus PO lines/shipments due before launch. Read shortfall.py (PartNeed.usable/gap/gap_if_acted, compute(), the plan_inbound loop that already handles "arrived" (at port) and "after_launch"), timing.py, and how cards.py builds the allocate/collect cards.

Fix: count inbound supply that will be in the DC before packing ends (ETA <= packing end / launch, status not cancelled, not already received into the stock snapshot (avoid double counting with goods_receipts after the snapshot date), and not contradicted by a document saying it is late or short; reuse what the linker/records give you) as available for the gap, separately visible (e.g. `need.arriving` list with reference, quantity, eta), so `gap` = needed - usable - arriving-in-time. Keep at_port (needs collecting) as a fix, not as available. Make sure the Hwaseong balance of 20,000 (arriving Tue 24 Nov, after launch) is NOT counted. Check the result on the real data: report the new numbers for CMP-GAM-001 and every other part that changed, and whether the allocate card still appears (it should only if a gap remains). Explain any remaining difference to the paper check's ~6,800.
Tests: add/adjust unit tests for the new rule; `uv run pytest -q` all pass; `uv run ruff check src tests --exclude tests/test_platform.py` clean. Final report: the change, before/after numbers, test results.

1	"""
     2	Price it: from the linked graph to copies at risk.
     3	
     4	For every edition still being packed: remaining = day-one demand - packed. For every part in
     5	its bill of materials: needed = remaining x quantity per copy. Usable stock = the latest book
     6	stock minus what the evidence says is not really there or can't be used (live linker issues with
     7	a stock effect). Gap = needed - usable. Everything comes from the data; nothing is typed in.
     8	"""
     9	
    10	import math
    11	import re
    12	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    13	from datetime import datetime, timedelta
    14	
    15	import pandas as pd
    16	
    17	from ask_soony.verifier.impact.timing import lead_hours, parse_moment, runs_dry, shift_windows
    18	
    19	# Linker issues whose units are book stock that is not really usable
    20	STOCK_EFFECT_RULES = {
    21	    "delivery_vs_receipt": "booked but not delivered",
    22	    "failed_lot_in_stock": "failed inspection",
    23	    "remark_names_other_part": "wrong part booked",
    24	    "old_revision_in_stock": "old revision, must not be packed",
    25	}
    26	
    27	
    28	@dataclass
    29	class Deduction:
    30	    reason: str
    31	    units: float
    32	    issue: str  # record id of the issue's record
    33	    context: str
    34	
    35	
    36	@dataclass
    37	class PartNeed:
    38	    part: str
    39	    description: str | None
    40	    editions: list[str]
    41	    needed: float
    42	    book_stock: float
    43	    book_as_of: str | None
    44	    deductions: list[Deduction] = field(default_factory=list)
    45	    plan_status: str | None = None  # what the launch plan says ('ok', 'CHECK')
    46	    supply: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)  # options to close the gap
    47	    per_copy: dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)  # edition → parts per copy
    48	    used_today: float | None = None
    49	    rate_per_hour: float | None = None  # how fast the lines use it
    50	    runs_dry: datetime | None = None  # None: lasts to the end of packing
    51	    fixes: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)  # supply that can arrive in time, with act-by
    52	
    53	    @property
    54	    def usable(self) -> float:
    55	        return max(self.book_stock - sum(d.units for d in self.deductions), 0)
    56	
    57	    @property
    58	    def gap(self) -> float:
    59	        return max(self.needed - self.usable, 0)
    60	
    61	    @property
    62	    def gap_if_acted(self) -> float:
    63	        """The gap left if every fix that can arrive in time is taken."""
    64	        closable = sum(f["quantity"] for f in self.fixes if f["in_time"])
    65	        return max(self.gap - closable, 0)
    66	
    67	
    68	@dataclass
    69	class Edition:
    70	    product: str
    71	    name: str | None
    72	    launch_date: str | None
    73	    day_one: float
    74	    packed: float
    75	    packed_as_of: str | None
    76	    rate_per_hour: float | None
    77	
    78	    @property
    79	    def remaining(self) -> float:
    80	        return max(self.day_one - self.packed, 0)
    81	
    82	
    83	@dataclass
    84	class Shortfall:
    85	    editions: list[Edition]
    86	    parts: list[PartNeed]
    87	    excluded: list[dict]  # BOM parts not stocked separately, with the evidence
    88	    now: datetime | None = None  # time of the newest stock figures
    89	    packing_ends: datetime | None = None
    90	    hours_left: float | None = None
    91	
    92	    def at_risk(self, product: str, acted: bool = False) -> tuple[float, str | None]:
    93	        """
    94	        Copies of an edition at risk from parts only it uses, and the part that binds.
    95	        acted=True: after every fix that can still arrive in time.
    96	        """
    97	
    98	        def gap(p: PartNeed) -> float:
    99	            return p.gap_if_acted if acted else p.gap
   100	
   101	        own = [p for p in self.parts if p.editions == [product] and gap(p) > 0]
   102	        if not own:
   103	            return 0, None
   104	        worst = max(own, key=gap)
   105	        return gap(worst), worst.part
   106	
   107	    @property
   108	    def shared_gaps(self) -> list[PartNeed]:
   109	        return [p for p in self.parts if len(p.editions) > 1 and p.gap > 0]
   110	
   111	
   112	def _latest(rows: list[dict]) -> dict | None:
   113	    """The newest record by as_of; records without a date come last."""
   114	    return max(rows, key=lambda r: r["as_of"] or "", default=None)
   115	
   116	
   117	def _known_parts(records: pd.DataFrame) -> set[str]:
   118	    return set(records[records.kind == "part"].material_id.dropna())
   119	
   120	
   121	def _fitted_parts(records: pd.DataFrame, known: set[str]) -> dict[str, dict]:
   122	    """
   123	    Parts a supplier says it fits into another part ('fitted by supplier into CMP-...'), so they
   124	    are never stocked on their own. Learned from the suppliers' own part lists.
   125	    """
   126	    fitted = {}
   127	    for r in records[records.kind == "supplier_part"].to_dict("records"):
   128	        note = r["attrs"].get("note") or ""
   129	        others = [p for p in known if p != r["material_id"] and re.search(re.escape(p), note)]
   130	        if others and re.search(r"fitted|included|built[- ]in|assembled", note, re.I):
   131	            fitted[r["material_id"]] = {
   132	                "inside": others[0],
   133	                "evidence": note,
   134	                "source": r["source"],
   135	            }
   136	    return fitted
   137	
   138	
   139	def compute(records: pd.DataFrame, issues: pd.DataFrame) -> Shortfall:
   140	    rows = records.to_dict("records")
   141	    by_kind: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
   142	    for r in rows:
   143	        by_kind.setdefault(r["kind"], []).append(r)
   144	
   145	    # Editions: launch products with a day-one demand
   146	    editions = []
   147	    for product in by_kind.get("product", []):
   148	        demand = product["attrs"].get("day_one_qty")
   149	        if not demand:
   150	            continue
   151	        pid = product["material_id"]
   152	        packed = _latest([r for r in by_kind.get("packed_count", []) if r["material_id"] == pid])
   153	        plans = [r for r in by_kind.get("plan_edition", []) if r["material_id"] == pid]
   154	        plan = _latest(plans)
   155	        packed_qty = (packed or {}).get("attrs", {}).get("quantity")
   156	        if packed_qty is None and plan:
   157	            packed_qty = plan["attrs"].get("packed")
   158	        rate = next(
   159	            (p["attrs"]["rate_per_hour"] for p in plans if p["attrs"].get("rate_per_hour")), None
   160	        )
   161	        editions.append(
   162	            Edition(
   163	                pid,
   164	                product["attrs"].get("name"),
   165	                product["attrs"].get("launch_date"),
   166	                demand,
   167	                packed_qty or 0,
   168	                (packed or plan or {}).get("as_of"),
   169	                rate,
   170	            )
   171	        )
   172	    remaining = {e.product: e.remaining for e in editions}
   173	
   174	    # Needs from the bill of materials
   175	    known = _known_parts(records)
   176	    fitted = _fitted_parts(records, known)
   177	    needs: dict[str, PartNeed] = {}
   178	    excluded = []
   179	    descriptions = {
   180	        r["material_id"]: r["attrs"].get("description") for r in by_kind.get("part", [])
   181	    }
   182	    for line in by_kind.get("bom_line", []):
   183	        parent, part = line["attrs"]["parent"], line["material_id"]
   184	        if parent not in remaining:
   185	            continue
   186	        if part in fitted:
   187	            excluded.append({"part": part, "edition": parent, **fitted[part]})
   188	            continue
   189	        need = needs.setdefault(part, PartNeed(part, descriptions.get(part), [], 0, 0, None))
   190	        need.editions.append(parent)
   191	        need.per_copy[parent] = line["attrs"].get("qty_per") or 1
   192	        need.needed += remaining[parent] * need.per_copy[parent]
   193	
   194	    # Book stock: the newest count per part; else the stock snapshot
   195	    for part, need in needs.items():
   196	        latest = _latest([r for r in by_kind.get("stock_count", []) if r["material_id"] == part])
   197	        if latest:
   198	            need.book_stock, need.book_as_of = latest["attrs"].get("quantity") or 0, latest["as_of"]
   199	            need.used_today = latest["attrs"].get("used_today")
   200	        else:
   201	            batches = [r for r in by_kind.get("stock_batch", []) if r["material_id"] == part]
   202	            need.book_stock = sum(r["attrs"].get("quantity") or 0 for r in batches)
   203	            need.book_as_of = _latest(batches)["as_of"] if batches else None
   204	        plan_part = _latest([r for r in by_kind.get("plan_part", []) if r["material_id"] == part])
   205	        need.plan_status = plan_part["attrs"].get("status") if plan_part else None
   206	
   207	    # Deductions: live issues with a stock effect
   208	    for issue in issues.to_dict("records"):
   209	        reason = STOCK_EFFECT_RULES.get(issue["rule"])
   210	        units = issue.get("units")
   211	        if (
   212	            not reason
   213	            or not issue.get("live")
   214	            or units is None
   215	            or (isinstance(units, float) and math.isnan(units))
   216	        ):
   217	            continue
   218	        if issue["material_id"] in needs:
   219	            needs[issue["material_id"]].deductions.append(
   220	                Deduction(reason, float(units), issue["record_id"], issue.get("context") or "")
   221	            )
   222	
   223	    # Supply that could close a gap before launch
   224	    launch = min((e.launch_date for e in editions if e.launch_date), default=None)
   225	    for plan in by_kind.get("plan_inbound", []):
   226	        need = needs.get(plan["material_id"])
   227	        status = (plan["attrs"].get("status") or "").lower()
   228	        if need is None:
   229	            continue
   230	        if "arrived" in status:  # at the port, not in stock yet: needs collecting
   231	            need.supply.append(
   232	                {
   233	                    "kind": "at_port",
   234	                    "quantity": plan["attrs"].get("quantity"),
   235	                    "reference": plan["reference"],
   236	                    "note": plan["attrs"].get("comment"),
   237	                    "supplier_id": plan["supplier_id"],
   238	                }
   239	            )
   240	        elif launch and plan["attrs"].get("eta") and plan["attrs"]["eta"] > launch:
   241	            need.supply.append(
   242	                {
   243	                    "kind": "after_launch",
   244	                    "quantity": plan["attrs"].get("quantity"),
   245	                    "reference": plan["reference"],
   246	                    "eta": plan["attrs"]["eta"],
   247	                    "supplier_id": plan["supplier_id"],
   248	                }
   249	            )
   250	    for reading in by_kind.get("reading", []):
   251	        if reading["attrs"].get("doc_type") != "offer":
   252	            continue
   253	        for line in (
   254	            r for r in by_kind.get("doc_line", []) if r["doc_path"] == reading["doc_path"]
   255	        ):
   256	            need = needs.get(line["material_id"])
   257	            final = line["attrs"]["final"]
   258	            quantity = next(
   259	                (
   260	                    final[k]
   261	                    for k in (
   262	                        "quantity_confirmed",
   263	                        "quantity_ordered",
   264	                        "quantity_shipped",
   265	                        "quantity_delivered",
   266	                    )
   267	                    if final.get(k)
   268	                ),
   269	                None,
   270	            )
   271	            if need is not None and quantity:
   272	                need.supply.append(
   273	                    {
   274	                        "kind": "offer",
   275	                        "quantity": quantity,
   276	                        "document": reading["doc_path"],
   277	                        "red_flags": reading["attrs"].get("red_flags", [])[:2],
   278	                        # 'loaded within 4 h of your order' + 'about 9 hours driving'
   279	                        "lead_texts": [
   280	                            v["raw"] for v in line["attrs"]["values"] if v["field"] == "lead_time"
   281	                        ]
   282	                        + [
   283	                            s["text_en"]
   284	                            for s in reading["attrs"].get("statements", [])
   285	                            if s.get("topic") == "shipment"
   286	                        ],
   287	                    }
   288	                )
   289	
   290	    parts = sorted(needs.values(), key=lambda p: -p.gap)
   291	    result = Shortfall(editions, parts, excluded)
   292	    _add_timing(result, by_kind, launch)
   293	    return result
   294	
   295	
   296	def _add_timing(result: Shortfall, by_kind: dict[str, list[dict]], launch: str | None) -> None:
   297	    """
   298	    When each part runs dry at the packing rate, and which fixes can arrive before then.
   299	
   300	    'Now' is the time of the newest stock or packed count. A fix's act-by time is when it must be
   301	    ordered or decided so it lands before the line runs dry.
   302	    """
   303	    windows = shift_windows([s["attrs"] for s in by_kind.get("plan_shift", [])], launch)
   304	    stamps = [
   305	        parse_moment(r["as_of"])
   306	        for kind in ("stock_count", "packed_count")
   307	        for r in by_kind.get(kind, [])
   308	        if r["as_of"]
   309	    ]
   310	    now = max((s for s in stamps if s), default=None)
   311	    if not windows or now is None:
   312	        return
   313	    result.now = now
   314	    result.packing_ends = windows[-1][1]
   315	    result.hours_left = (
   316	        sum(max((end - max(start, now)).total_seconds(), 0) for start, end in windows) / 3600
   317	    )
   318	    rates = {e.product: e.rate_per_hour for e in result.editions}
   319	    for need in result.parts:
   320	        rate = sum((rates.get(e) or 0) * q for e, q in need.per_copy.items())
   321	        need.rate_per_hour = rate or None
   322	        if rate:
   323	            need.runs_dry = runs_dry(windows, now, need.usable / rate)
   324	        deadline = need.runs_dry or result.packing_ends
   325	        if not need.gap:
   326	            continue
   327	        for supply in need.supply:
   328	            if supply["kind"] == "at_port":
   329	                need.fixes.append(
   330	                    {
   331	                        "kind": "collect",
   332	                        "quantity": min(supply["quantity"] or 0, need.gap),
   333	                        "available": supply["quantity"],
   334	                        "act_by": deadline,
   335	                        "arrives": None,
   336	                        "in_time": True,
   337	                        "reference": supply.get("reference"),
   338	                        "assumption": "collected and unloaded before the line runs dry",
   339	                    }
   340	                )
   341	            elif supply["kind"] == "offer":
   342	                lead = lead_hours(supply.get("lead_texts", []))
   343	                arrives = now + timedelta(hours=lead) if lead is not None else None
   344	                in_time = arrives is not None and arrives <= result.packing_ends
   345	                need.fixes.append(
   346	                    {
   347	                        "kind": "order",
   348	                        "quantity": min(supply["quantity"], need.gap),
   349	                        "available": supply["quantity"],
   350	                        "lead_hours": lead,
   351	                        "act_by": deadline - timedelta(hours=lead) if lead is not None else None,
   352	                        "arrives": arrives,
   353	                        "in_time": in_time,
   354	                        "document": supply.get("document"),
   355	                    }
   356	                )
   357	        for deduction in need.deductions:
   358	            if deduction.reason == "failed inspection":
   359	                need.fixes.append(
   360	                    {
   361	                        "kind": "concession",
   362	                        "quantity": min(deduction.units, need.gap),
   363	                        "available": deduction.units,
   364	                        "act_by": deadline,
   365	                        "arrives": None,
   366	                        "in_time": True,
   367	                        "issue": deduction.issue,
   368	                    }
   369	                )
     1	"""
     2	When does a part run out, and by when must someone act?
     3	
     4	Packing time comes from the launch plan's shift table ('Saturday 06:00–22:00'), placed on the
     5	days before launch. 'Now' is the time of the newest stock figures, not the machine clock, so the
     6	answer is the same every time the same data is read. All times are the DC's clock as written.
     7	"""
     8	
     9	import re
    10	from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta
    11	
    12	_TIMES = re.compile(r"(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})\s*[–—-]\s*(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})")
    13	_HOURS = re.compile(r"(\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)\s*(?:h\b|hrs?\b|hours?\b|godz)", re.I)
    14	WEEKDAYS = ["monday", "tuesday", "wednesday", "thursday", "friday", "saturday", "sunday"]
    15	
    16	
    17	def parse_moment(value: str | None) -> datetime | None:
    18	    """An ISO timestamp from the records (always UTC 'Z' form) as a naive datetime."""
    19	    if not value:
    20	        return None
    21	    try:
    22	        return datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "")).replace(tzinfo=None)
    23	    except ValueError:
    24	        return None
    25	
    26	
    27	def shift_windows(shifts: list[dict], launch_date: str | None) -> list[tuple[datetime, datetime]]:
    28	    """
    29	    Packing windows from rows like {'day': 'Saturday', 'shift': '06:00–22:00'}: each weekday is
    30	    placed on its date within the 7 days up to and including launch day.
    31	    """
    32	    if not launch_date:
    33	        return []
    34	    launch = date.fromisoformat(launch_date)
    35	    windows = []
    36	    for shift in shifts:
    37	        day = (shift.get("day") or "").strip().lower()
    38	        match = _TIMES.search(shift.get("shift") or "")
    39	        if day not in WEEKDAYS or not match:
    40	            continue
    41	        offset = (launch.weekday() - WEEKDAYS.index(day)) % 7
    42	        on = launch - timedelta(days=offset)
    43	        h1, m1, h2, m2 = map(int, match.groups())
    44	        start = datetime(on.year, on.month, on.day, h1, m1)
    45	        end = datetime(on.year, on.month, on.day, h2, m2)
    46	        windows.append((start, end))
    47	    return sorted(windows)
    48	
    49	
    50	def hours_left(windows: list[tuple[datetime, datetime]], now: datetime) -> float:
    51	    return sum(max((end - max(start, now)).total_seconds(), 0) for start, end in windows) / 3600
    52	
    53	
    54	def runs_dry(

     2	When does a part run out, and by when must someone act?
     3	
     4	Packing time comes from the launch plan's shift table ('Saturday 06:00–22:00'), placed on the
     5	days before launch. 'Now' is the time of the newest stock figures, not the machine clock, so the
     6	answer is the same every time the same data is read. All times are the DC's clock as written.
     7	"""
     8	
     9	import re
    10	from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta
    11	
    12	_TIMES = re.compile(r"(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})\s*[–—-]\s*(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})")
    13	_HOURS = re.compile(r"(\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)\s*(?:h\b|hrs?\b|hours?\b|godz)", re.I)
    14	WEEKDAYS = ["monday", "tuesday", "wednesday", "thursday", "friday", "saturday", "sunday"]
    15	
    16	
    17	def parse_moment(value: str | None) -> datetime | None:
    18	    """An ISO timestamp from the records (always UTC 'Z' form) as a naive datetime."""
    19	    if not value:
    20	        return None
    21	    try:
    22	        return datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "")).replace(tzinfo=None)
    23	    except ValueError:
    24	        return None
    25	
    26	
    27	def shift_windows(shifts: list[dict], launch_date: str | None) -> list[tuple[datetime, datetime]]:
    28	    """
    29	    Packing windows from rows like {'day': 'Saturday', 'shift': '06:00–22:00'}: each weekday is
    30	    placed on its date within the 7 days up to and including launch day.
    31	    """
    32	    if not launch_date:
    33	        return []
    34	    launch = date.fromisoformat(launch_date)
    35	    windows = []
    36	    for shift in shifts:
    37	        day = (shift.get("day") or "").strip().lower()
    38	        match = _TIMES.search(shift.get("shift") or "")
    39	        if day not in WEEKDAYS or not match:
    40	            continue
    41	        offset = (launch.weekday() - WEEKDAYS.index(day)) % 7
    42	        on = launch - timedelta(days=offset)
    43	        h1, m1, h2, m2 = map(int, match.groups())
    44	        start = datetime(on.year, on.month, on.day, h1, m1)
    45	        end = datetime(on.year, on.month, on.day, h2, m2)
    46	        windows.append((start, end))
    47	    return sorted(windows)

    51	    return sum(max((end - max(start, now)).total_seconds(), 0) for start, end in windows) / 3600

    58	    left = packing_hours

    61	        if begin >= end:
    62	            continue
    63	        available = (end - begin).total_seconds() / 3600
    64	        if left <= available:
    65	            return begin + timedelta(hours=left)
    66	        left -= available
    67	    return None

    79	        found = [float(m.replace(",", ".")) for m in _HOURS.findall(text or "")]
    80	        if found:
    81	            per_text.append(max(found))
    82	    return sum(per_text) if per_text else None

"""
Build the link graph from the portal data, save it, and trace one order through it.
"""

import json
import sqlite3
from collections import deque
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

from ask_soony.verifier.linker.adapters import ADAPTERS, PROFILE_KINDS, Context
from ask_soony.verifier.linker.adapters.readings import load_readings, map_supplier_part_numbers
from ask_soony.verifier.linker.discover import Source, discover
from ask_soony.verifier.linker.normalize import SupplierResolver
from ask_soony.verifier.linker.records import HUB_KINDS, RECORD_COLUMNS, disambiguate
from ask_soony.verifier.linker.rules import apply_all


@dataclass
class Graph:
    sources: pd.DataFrame  # path, kind, sha256, adapter, records, error
    records: pd.DataFrame
    links: pd.DataFrame
    issues: pd.DataFrame
    coverage: pd.DataFrame
    built_at: str


def _run(source: Source, ctx: Context) -> tuple[list[dict], dict]:
    adapter = ADAPTERS.get(source.kind)
    row = {
        "path": source.path,
        "kind": source.kind,
        "sha256": source.sha256,
        "adapter": adapter is not None,
        "records": 0,
        "error": source.meta.get("error"),
    }

def check_shipped_against_ordered(records: pd.DataFrame, links: pd.DataFrame) -> list[dict]:
    """
    A supplier's shipping document says less was shipped than the PO line holds.

    The line is the PO line whose quantity matches the 'ordered' figure on the paper; without
    one, the only candidate for that part. Delivery notes for the same PO and part are named.
    """
    lookup, issues = _Readings(records, links), []
    for reading_id, doc_id in lookup.doc_of.items():
        if lookup.by_id[doc_id]["kind"] != "shipping_doc":
            continue
        for line in lookup.lines_of.get(reading_id, []):
            final = line["attrs"]["final"]
            shipped = final.get("quantity_shipped")
            candidates = lookup.po_lines_of.get(line["record_id"], [])
            if shipped is None or not candidates:
                continue
            ordered_paper = final.get("quantity_ordered")
            matching = [
                c
                for c in candidates
                if ordered_paper is not None
                and abs((c["attrs"].get("quantity") or 0) - ordered_paper) < 0.5
            ]
            chosen = matching or (candidates if len(candidates) == 1 else [])
            if len(chosen) != 1:
                continue
            po_line = chosen[0]
            ordered = po_line["attrs"].get("quantity") or 0
            if shipped >= ordered - 0.5:
                continue
            expected = [v["raw"] for v in line["attrs"]["values"] if v["field"] == "date_expected"]
            context = (
                f"{line['material_id']}: shipped {_fmt(shipped)} of {_fmt(ordered)}"
                f", balance {_fmt(final.get('quantity_balance', ordered - shipped))}"
            )
            if expected:
                context += f", expected {expected[-1]}"
            notes = [
                f"{other['delivery_note'] or other['doc_path'].rsplit('/', 1)[-1]} received "
                f"{_fmt(_paper_quantity(dl)[0])}"
                for other in lookup.readings
                if other["record_id"] != reading_id
                and lookup.by_id.get(lookup.doc_of.get(other["record_id"], ""), {}).get("kind")
                == "delivery_note_scan"
                and po_line["po_number"] in (other["po_numbers"] or [])
                for dl in lookup.lines_of.get(other["record_id"], [])
                if dl["material_id"] == line["material_id"] and _paper_quantity(dl)[0] is not None
            ]
            if notes:
                context += "; delivery notes: " + ", ".join(notes)
            issues.append(
                _issue(
                    "shipped_vs_ordered",
                    "conflict",
                    po_line["record_id"],
                    "Supplier shipped less than the PO line",
                    doc_id,
                    context,
                )
            )
    return issues


def doc_name(doc: dict) -> str:
    return (doc.get("doc_path") or "").rsplit("/", 1)[-1]


def check_old_revision_in_stock(records: pd.DataFrame, links: pd.DataFrame) -> list[dict]:
    """
    A change notice says the old revision of a part must not be packed. A supplier's
    confirmation says its PO was made to that old revision, and that PO's receipt is still a
    batch in stock: that stock can't be used.
    """
    lookup, issues = _Readings(records, links), []
    changes = [
        r
        for r in lookup.by_id.values()
        if r["kind"] == "bom_change"
        and (r["attrs"].get("use_up_old_rev") or "").upper() == "N"
        and r["attrs"].get("rev_old")
    ]
    if not changes:
        return []
    stock = {r["batch"]: r for r in lookup.by_id.values() if r["kind"] == "stock_batch"}
    receipts_by_po: dict[tuple, list[dict]] = {}
    for r in lookup.by_id.values():
        if r["kind"] == "goods_receipt" and r["po_number"]:
            receipts_by_po.setdefault((r["po_number"], r["material_id"]), []).append(r)
    for change in changes:
        part, old = change["material_id"], change["attrs"]["rev_old"]
        says_old = re.compile(rf"\brev(?:ision|\.)?\s*{re.escape(old)}\b", re.I)
        for reading_id, doc_id in lookup.doc_of.items():
            doc = lookup.by_id[doc_id]
            if doc["kind"] not in ("confirmation", "shipping_doc"):
                continue
            statements = lookup.by_id[reading_id]["attrs"].get("statements") or []
            if not any(says_old.search(s.get("text_en") or "") for s in statements):
                continue
            for receipt in receipts_by_po.get((doc["po_number"], part), []):
                batch = stock.get(receipt["gr_number"])
                if batch is None or (batch["attrs"].get("quantity") or 0) <= 0:
                    continue
                quantity = batch["attrs"]["quantity"]
                issues.append(
                    _issue(
                        "old_revision_in_stock",
                        "conflict",
                        batch["record_id"],
                        "Stock is an old revision that must not be packed",
                        change["record_id"],
                        f"{quantity:,.0f} of {part} rev {old} (per {doc_name(doc)}); "
                        f"{change['key']}: {change['attrs'].get('reason')}",
                        part,
                        quantity,
                    )
                )
    # One issue per batch, even if several documents say the same
    seen, unique = set(), []
    for issue in issues:
        if issue["record_id"] not in seen:
            seen.add(issue["record_id"])
            unique.append(issue)
    return unique


def check_plan_inbound_against_paper(records: pd.DataFrame, links: pd.DataFrame) -> list[dict]:
    """
    The launch plan expects an inbound quantity by a date; the supplier's shipping document for
    the same air waybill or container says less, or later.
    """
    lookup, issues = _Readings(records, links), []
    docs_by_ref: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    for reading_id, doc_id in lookup.doc_of.items():
        doc = lookup.by_id[doc_id]
        if doc["kind"] == "shipping_doc" and doc["reference"]:
            docs_by_ref.setdefault(doc["reference"], []).append(lookup.by_id[reading_id])
    for plan in (r for r in lookup.by_id.values() if r["kind"] == "plan_inbound"):
        for reading in docs_by_ref.get(plan["reference"], []):
            for line in lookup.lines_of.get(reading["record_id"], []):
                if line["material_id"] != plan["material_id"]:
                    continue
                shipped = line["attrs"]["final"].get("quantity_shipped")
                expected = [
                    v["raw"] for v in line["attrs"]["values"] if v["field"] == "date_expected"
                ]
                planned = plan["attrs"].get("quantity") or 0
                if shipped is None or shipped >= planned - 0.5:
                    continue
                context = (
                    f"{plan['material_id']} via {plan['reference']}: plan {planned:,.0f} by "
                    f"{plan['attrs'].get('eta')}, supplier shipped {shipped:,.0f}"
                    + (f"; balance expected {expected[-1]}" if expected else "")
                )
                issues.append(
                    _issue(
                        "plan_vs_paper",
                        "conflict",
                        plan["record_id"],
                        "Launch plan expects more than the supplier shipped",
                        reading["record_id"],
                        context,
                        plan["material_id"],
                        planned - shipped,
                    )
                )
    return issues

            receipts_by_po.setdefault((r["po_number"], r["material_id"]), []).append(r)
    for change in changes:
        part, old = change["material_id"], change["attrs"]["rev_old"]
        says_old = re.compile(rf"\brev(?:ision|\.)?\s*{re.escape(old)}\b", re.I)
        for reading_id, doc_id in lookup.doc_of.items():
            doc = lookup.by_id[doc_id]
            if doc["kind"] not in ("confirmation", "shipping_doc"):
                continue
            statements = lookup.by_id[reading_id]["attrs"].get("statements") or []
            if not any(says_old.search(s.get("text_en") or "") for s in statements):
                continue
            for receipt in receipts_by_po.get((doc["po_number"], part), []):
                batch = stock.get(receipt["gr_number"])
                if batch is None or (batch["attrs"].get("quantity") or 0) <= 0:
                    continue
                quantity = batch["attrs"]["quantity"]
                issues.append(
                    _issue(
                        "old_revision_in_stock",
                        "conflict",
                        batch["record_id"],
                        "Stock is an old revision that must not be packed",
                        change["record_id"],
                        f"{quantity:,.0f} of {part} rev {old} (per {doc_name(doc)}); "
                        f"{change['key']}: {change['attrs'].get('reason')}",
                        part,
                        quantity,
                    )
                )
    # One issue per batch, even if several documents say the same
    seen, unique = set(), []
    for issue in issues:
        if issue["record_id"] not in seen:
            seen.add(issue["record_id"])
            unique.append(issue)
    return unique


def check_plan_inbound_against_paper(records: pd.DataFrame, links: pd.DataFrame) -> list[dict]:
    """
    The launch plan expects an inbound quantity by a date; the supplier's shipping document for
    the same air waybill or container says less, or later.
    """
    lookup, issues = _Readings(records, links), []
    docs_by_ref: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    for reading_id, doc_id in lookup.doc_of.items():
        doc = lookup.by_id[doc_id]
        if doc["kind"] == "shipping_doc" and doc["reference"]:
            docs_by_ref.setdefault(doc["reference"], []).append(lookup.by_id[reading_id])
    for plan in (r for r in lookup.by_id.values() if r["kind"] == "plan_inbound"):
        for reading in docs_by_ref.get(plan["reference"], []):
            for line in lookup.lines_of.get(reading["record_id"], []):
                if line["material_id"] != plan["material_id"]:
                    continue
                shipped = line["attrs"]["final"].get("quantity_shipped")
                expected = [
                    v["raw"] for v in line["attrs"]["values"] if v["field"] == "date_expected"
                ]
                planned = plan["attrs"].get("quantity") or 0
                if shipped is None or shipped >= planned - 0.5:
                    continue
                context = (
                    f"{plan['material_id']} via {plan['reference']}: plan {planned:,.0f} by "
                    f"{plan['attrs'].get('eta')}, supplier shipped {shipped:,.0f}"
                    + (f"; balance expected {expected[-1]}" if expected else "")
                )
                issues.append(
                    _issue(
                        "plan_vs_paper",
                        "conflict",
                        plan["record_id"],
                        "Launch plan expects more than the supplier shipped",
                        reading["record_id"],
                        context,
                        plan["material_id"],
                        planned - shipped,
                    )
                )
    return issues


FAILED = {"fail", "rejected"}

# Image recognizer (discovery run)

Reads every document (scans, photos, PDFs) with one OpenAI vision call each (`OPENAI_API_KEY` from `.env`). Images are resized and PDF pages without a text layer are rendered to images by the shared `ask_soony.extract`; the answer is forced into the JSON schema in `schema.py`. The goal is to see what the documents say and what kinds of errors keep coming up.

```bash
uv run python -m ask_soony.verifier.image_recognizer                       # all ~277 documents, resumable
uv run python -m ask_soony.verifier.image_recognizer --only WZ-261116-473   # one document
uv run python -m ask_soony.verifier.image_recognizer --images-only --limit 5
```

Options: `--model` (default `gpt-5.4-mini`), `--effort` (default `medium`), `--concurrency` (default 4), `--force` (read again).

## Output: `data/store/image_recognizer/` (gitignored, confidential)

One folder per document, `<path>__<sha12>/`:

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `verdict.json` | Everything on the paper as values: raw text **and** a plain `number` (`80.000` → 80000), printed/handwritten/stamped, crossed out, legible. Plus references, statements, `decisions` (inspection pass/fail, approvals), corrections, and the verdict (status, red flags, observations) |
| `meta.json` | Checksum, model, time, token usage, status, error |

Plus `index.jsonl` (one line per document read) and `run_summary.json` (counts by type, verdict and status, plus errors).

## Behaviour

- **Resumable:** results are keyed by file checksum. Stop any time, and the next run skips what's done. A changed file is read again.
- **Isolated:** one call, no tools; the prompt treats document text as data.
- **Retries:** 2 retries for API or process errors. Refusals and schema failures aren't retried; they're logged and skipped.

- Real cards: verifier (branch origin/verifier) must write cards with real supplier addresses + drafts in `messages`; otherwise send_supplier_email correctly refuses (example addresses).

1. Ask user which comes first: verifier cards integration vs. auto-escalation; ask whether to push jonas/alerts and jonas/voice-dashboard once GitHub is reachable; tell Akshat about the branch.
2. Wire critical cards -> push -> (no answer) -> Twilio/gpt-realtime call, decision into decisions.json.
3. Retest phone call with VAD 0.8 and iPhone Voice Isolation; test PWA push end to end.
4. Demo script, deck, 3-min video before 11:30; README for hand-in.

"""
Readings (M3): what the image recognizer read from each document, as linker records.

One 'reading' record per document (keys from the references inside it) and one 'doc_line' record
per line on it (part and values). Fixes for known reader errors are applied here, on load:
- counts are re-parsed from the raw text ('19.000' is 19000, see normalize.count_number)
- corrections are derived from the values (crossed out or handwritten), not taken from the
  reader's own list, which mostly holds signatures and stamps
- supplier part numbers are mapped to the buyer's (map_supplier_part_numbers)

The raw text of every value is kept next to the number, so nothing the reader saw is lost.
"""

import hashlib
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from ask_soony.verifier.linker.normalize import clean, count_number
from ask_soony.verifier.linker.records import make_record

REFERENCE_KEYS = {
    "po_number": "po_numbers",
    "delivery_note": "delivery_note",
    "air_waybill": "reference",
    "container": "reference",
    "batch": "batch",
    "goods_receipt": "batch",  # a goods receipt number is the batch number
}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ReadingSource:
    """Where a reading came from, shaped like a discovered Source for make_record."""

    path: str
    sha256: str


def _references(verdict: dict) -> dict:
    keys: dict = {"po_numbers": []}
    for ref in verdict.get("references") or []:
        column = REFERENCE_KEYS.get(ref.get("type"))
        value = clean(ref.get("value"))
        if column is None or value is None:
            continue

"""Shortfall and decision cards on a made-up portal (see verifier/linker/tests/conftest.py)."""

import hashlib
import json

import openpyxl

from ask_soony.dispatch.decisions.cards import build_cards
from ask_soony.verifier.impact.shortfall import compute
from ask_soony.verifier.linker import build
from ask_soony.verifier.linker.tests.conftest import make_portal, write

REPORT = "soony/receiving/DC-X/inspection_report_7000000001.pdf"


def portal_with_plan(tmp_path):
    root = make_portal(tmp_path / "portal")
    write(
        root,
        "soony/master/products.csv",
        "product_id,name,lifecycle,launch_date,weekly_plan_qty,day_one_qty\n"
        "FG-1,Edition One,launch,2026-03-01,10,1000\nFG-2,Edition Two,launch,2026-03-01,10,100",
    )
    write(
        root,
        "soony/master/bom.csv",
        "parent_id,child_id,qty_per,valid_from,valid_to\n"
        "FG-1,CMP-A,1,2024-01-01,9999-12-31\nFG-2,CMP-A,1,2024-01-01,9999-12-31\n"
        "FG-2,CMP-B,2,2024-01-01,9999-12-31\nFG-2,CMP-MAG,4,2024-01-01,9999-12-31",
    )
    write(
        root,
        "suppliers/SUP-0007_Acme_Parts/components.csv",
        "component_id,description,category,share,unit_price,currency,lead_time_days,moq,primary,note\n"
        "CMP-B,Part B,Cat,1,2.0,EUR,10,1,Y,\n"
        "CMP-MAG,Magnet,Cat,1,0,EUR,10,0,Y,fitted by supplier into CMP-B; not stocked separately",
    )
    # Stock update workbook: two tables on two sheets, counts written with dot thousands
    wb = openpyxl.Workbook()
    ws = wb.active
    ws.title = "Components"
    ws.append(["Stock after receipts 2026-02-28, late shift (book stock)"])
    ws.append(
        [
            "Site",
            "Material",
            "Description",
            "Qty",
            "UoM",
            "Receipts today",
            "Used today",
            "Last count",
        ]
    )
    ws.append(["DC-X", "CMP-A", "Part A", "1.050", "PC", 0, 0, "2026-02-28"])
    ws.append(["DC-X", "CMP-B", "Part B", "400", "PC", 0, 0, "2026-02-28"])
    fg = wb.create_sheet("Finished goods")
    fg.append(["Packed copies DC-X, 2026-02-28 20:00"])
    fg.append(["Site", "Material", "Description", "Qty", "UoM", "Packed today", "Last count"])
    fg.append(["DC-X", "FG-1", "Edition One", "500", "PC", 0, "2026-02-28"])
    fg.append(["DC-X", "FG-2", "Edition Two", "0", "PC", 0, "2026-02-28"])
    (root / "soony/erp").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    wb.save(root / "soony/erp/stock_update.xlsx")
    return root


def failed_inspection(root, readings):
    folder = readings / "report"
    folder.mkdir(parents=True)
    sha = hashlib.sha256((root / REPORT).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    (folder / "meta.json").write_text(json.dumps({"path": REPORT, "sha256": sha, "status": "ok"}))
    (folder / "verdict.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "document_type": "inspection_report",
                "references": [],
                "lines": [],
                "statements": [],
                "corrections": [],
                "decisions": [
                    {
                        "subject": "lot",
                        "outcome": "fail",
                        "decided_by": None,
                        "conditions": None,
                        "quote": "fail",
                    }
                ],
                "verdict": {
                    "status": "has_warnings",
                    "summary_en": "",
                    "red_flags": [],
                    "confidence": "high",
                    "observations": [],
                },
            }
        )
    )


def test_needs_come_from_demand_packed_and_bom(tmp_path):
    root = portal_with_plan(tmp_path)
    graph = build(root)
    result = compute(graph.records, graph.issues)
    remaining = {e.product: e.remaining for e in result.editions}
    assert remaining == {"FG-1": 500, "FG-2": 100}  # packed count from the stock update
    needs = {p.part: p for p in result.parts}
    assert needs["CMP-A"].needed == 600  # shared: 500 + 100
    assert needs["CMP-B"].needed == 200  # 2 per copy of FG-2
    assert needs["CMP-A"].book_stock == 1050  # '1.050' is a thousands group
    assert "CMP-MAG" not in needs  # fitted inside CMP-B by the supplier, never stocked
    assert [x["part"] for x in result.excluded] == ["CMP-MAG"]


def test_failed_lot_is_not_usable_and_puts_copies_at_risk(tmp_path):
    root = portal_with_plan(tmp_path)
    readings = tmp_path / "readings"
    failed_inspection(root, readings)
    graph = build(root, readings)
    result = compute(graph.records, graph.issues)
    part_a = next(p for p in result.parts if p.part == "CMP-A")
    assert [d.reason for d in part_a.deductions] == ["failed inspection"]
    assert part_a.usable == 1050 - 500  # batch 7000000001 holds 500
    assert part_a.gap == 50
    assert result.shared_gaps == [part_a]  # CMP-A is used by both editions


def test_decisions_route_to_the_correct_approver(tmp_path):
    root = portal_with_plan(tmp_path)
    readings = tmp_path / "readings"
    failed_inspection(root, readings)
    graph = build(root, readings)
    result = compute(graph.records, graph.issues)
    cards = build_cards(result, graph.issues, graph.records)
    concession = next(c for c in cards if c.id == "concession-CMP-A")
    assert concession.decision
    # No org chart in this portal: the card names the role to find, not a person
    assert concession.messages[0].to_role == "approver of exceptions (see the approval policy)"


def test_cards_carry_deadlines_and_before_after(tmp_path):
    root = portal_with_plan(tmp_path)
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(root / "soony/erp/stock_update.xlsx")
    shifts = wb.create_sheet("Shifts")
    shifts.append(["Day", "Shift", "Hours", "Lines"])
    shifts.append(["Sunday", "06:00–20:00", 14, "L1"])  # launch day is Sun 1 Mar 2026
    wb.save(root / "soony/erp/stock_update.xlsx")
    write(
        root,
        "soony/master/products.csv",
        "product_id,name,lifecycle,launch_date,weekly_plan_qty,day_one_qty\n"
        "FG-1,Edition One,launch,2026-03-01,10,1000\nFG-2,Edition Two,launch,2026-03-01,10,100",
    )
    readings = tmp_path / "readings"
    failed_inspection(root, readings)
    graph = build(root, readings)
    result = compute(graph.records, graph.issues)
    # No packing rate in this plan, so no run-out time; the concession still closes the gap
    part_a = next(p for p in result.parts if p.part == "CMP-A")
    assert part_a.gap == 50 and part_a.gap_if_acted == 0
    cards = build_cards(result, graph.issues, graph.records)
    concession = next(c for c in cards if c.id == "concession-CMP-A")
    assert (concession.at_risk, concession.at_risk_if_acted) == (50, 0)


def test_blocked_stock_card_asks_whether_it_was_packed(tmp_path):
    root = portal_with_plan(tmp_path)
    receipts = root / "soony/erp/goods_receipts.csv"
    receipts.write_text(
        receipts.read_text()
        + '7000000020,2026-02-20,9100000002,1,SUP-0007,CMP-B,DC-X,200,200,WZ-1,Insp,"1 pallet holds CMP-A (10 pcs)"\n'
    )
    graph = build(root)
    result = compute(graph.records, graph.issues)
    cards = build_cards(result, graph.issues, graph.records)
    blocked = next(c for c in cards if c.id.startswith("wrong"))
    assert blocked.blocked_only and blocked.at_risk == 0
    assert "do any packed copies already contain this stock?" in blocked.messages[0].body

from ask_soony.dispatch.decisions.cards import build_cards
from ask_soony.verifier.impact.shortfall import compute
from ask_soony.verifier.linker import build
from ask_soony.verifier.linker.tests.conftest import make_portal, write

REPORT = "soony/receiving/DC-X/inspection_report_7000000001.pdf"


def portal_with_plan(tmp_path):
    root = make_portal(tmp_path / "portal")
    write(
        root,
        "soony/master/products.csv",
        "product_id,name,lifecycle,launch_date,weekly_plan_qty,day_one_qty\n"
        "FG-1,Edition One,launch,2026-03-01,10,1000\nFG-2,Edition Two,launch,2026-03-01,10,100",
    )
    write(
        root,
        "soony/master/bom.csv",
        "parent_id,child_id,qty_per,valid_from,valid_to\n"
        "FG-1,CMP-A,1,2024-01-01,9999-12-31\nFG-2,CMP-A,1,2024-01-01,9999-12-31\n"
        "FG-2,CMP-B,2,2024-01-01,9999-12-31\nFG-2,CMP-MAG,4,2024-01-01,9999-12-31",
    )
    write(
        root,
        "suppliers/SUP-0007_Acme_Parts/components.csv",
        "component_id,description,category,share,unit_price,currency,lead_time_days,moq,primary,note\n"
        "CMP-B,Part B,Cat,1,2.0,EUR,10,1,Y,\n"
        "CMP-MAG,Magnet,Cat,1,0,EUR,10,0,Y,fitted by supplier into CMP-B; not stocked separately",
    )
    # Stock update workbook: two tables on two sheets, counts written with dot thousands
    wb = openpyxl.Workbook()
    ws = wb.active
    ws.title = "Components"
    ws.append(["Stock after receipts 2026-02-28, late shift (book stock)"])
    ws.append(
        [
            "Site",
            "Material",
            "Description",
            "Qty",
            "UoM",
            "Receipts today",
            "Used today",
            "Last count",
        ]
    )
    ws.append(["DC-X", "CMP-A", "Part A", "1.050", "PC", 0, 0, "2026-02-28"])
    ws.append(["DC-X", "CMP-B", "Part B", "400", "PC", 0, 0, "2026-02-28"])
    fg = wb.create_sheet("Finished goods")
    fg.append(["Packed copies DC-X, 2026-02-28 20:00"])
    fg.append(["Site", "Material", "Description", "Qty", "UoM", "Packed today", "Last count"])
    fg.append(["DC-X", "FG-1", "Edition One", "500", "PC", 0, "2026-02-28"])
    fg.append(["DC-X", "FG-2", "Edition Two", "0", "PC", 0, "2026-02-28"])
    (root / "soony/erp").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    wb.save(root / "soony/erp/stock_update.xlsx")
    return root


def failed_inspection(root, readings):
    folder = readings / "report"
    folder.mkdir(parents=True)
    sha = hashlib.sha256((root / REPORT).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    (folder / "meta.json").write_text(json.dumps({"path": REPORT, "sha256": sha, "status": "ok"}))
    (folder / "verdict.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "document_type": "inspection_report",
                "references": [],
                "lines": [],
                "statements": [],
                "corrections": [],
                "decisions": [
                    {
                        "subject": "lot",
                        "outcome": "fail",
                        "decided_by": None,
                        "conditions": None,
                        "quote": "fail",
                    }
                ],
                "verdict": {
                    "status": "has_warnings",
                    "summary_en": "",
                    "red_flags": [],
                    "confidence": "high",
                    "observations": [],
                },
            }
        )
    )


def test_needs_come_from_demand_packed_and_bom(tmp_path):
    root = portal_with_plan(tmp_path)
    graph = build(root)
    result = compute(graph.records, graph.issues)
    remaining = {e.product: e.remaining for e in result.editions}
    assert remaining == {"FG-1": 500, "FG-2": 100}  # packed count from the stock update
    needs = {p.part: p for p in result.parts}
    assert needs["CMP-A"].needed == 600  # shared: 500 + 100
    assert needs["CMP-B"].needed == 200  # 2 per copy of FG-2
    assert needs["CMP-A"].book_stock == 1050  # '1.050' is a thousands group
    assert "CMP-MAG" not in needs  # fitted inside CMP-B by the supplier, never stocked
    assert [x["part"] for x in result.excluded] == ["CMP-MAG"]


def test_failed_lot_is_not_usable_and_puts_copies_at_risk(tmp_path):
    root = portal_with_plan(tmp_path)
    readings = tmp_path / "readings"
    failed_inspection(root, readings)
    graph = build(root, readings)
    result = compute(graph.records, graph.issues)
    part_a = next(p for p in result.parts if p.part == "CMP-A")
    assert [d.reason for d in part_a.deductions] == ["failed inspection"]
    assert part_a.usable == 1050 - 500  # batch 7000000001 holds 500
    assert part_a.gap == 50
    assert result.shared_gaps == [part_a]  # CMP-A is used by both editions


def test_decisions_route_to_the_correct_approver(tmp_path):
    root = portal_with_plan(tmp_path)
    readings = tmp_path / "readings"
    failed_inspection(root, readings)
    graph = build(root, readings)
    result = compute(graph.records, graph.issues)
    cards = build_cards(result, graph.issues, graph.records)
    concession = next(c for c in cards if c.id == "concession-CMP-A")
    assert concession.decision
    # No org chart in this portal: the card names the role to find, not a person
    assert concession.messages[0].to_role == "approver of exceptions (see the approval policy)"


def test_cards_carry_deadlines_and_before_after(tmp_path):
    root = portal_with_plan(tmp_path)
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(root / "soony/erp/stock_update.xlsx")
    shifts = wb.create_sheet("Shifts")
    shifts.append(["Day", "Shift", "Hours", "Lines"])
    shifts.append(["Sunday", "06:00–20:00", 14, "L1"])  # launch day is Sun 1 Mar 2026
    wb.save(root / "soony/erp/stock_update.xlsx")
    write(
        root,
        "soony/master/products.csv",
        "product_id,name,lifecycle,launch_date,weekly_plan_qty,day_one_qty\n"
        "FG-1,Edition One,launch,2026-03-01,10,1000\nFG-2,Edition Two,launch,2026-03-01,10,100",
    )
    readings = tmp_path / "readings"
    failed_inspection(root, readings)
    graph = build(root, readings)
    result = compute(graph.records, graph.issues)
    # No packing rate in this plan, so no run-out time; the concession still closes the gap
    part_a = next(p for p in result.parts if p.part == "CMP-A")
    assert part_a.gap == 50 and part_a.gap_if_acted == 0
    cards = build_cards(result, graph.issues, graph.records)
    concession = next(c for c in cards if c.id == "concession-CMP-A")
    assert (concession.at_risk, concession.at_risk_if_acted) == (50, 0)


def test_blocked_stock_card_asks_whether_it_was_packed(tmp_path):
    root = portal_with_plan(tmp_path)
    receipts = root / "soony/erp/goods_receipts.csv"
    receipts.write_text(
        receipts.read_text()
        + '7000000020,2026-02-20,9100000002,1,SUP-0007,CMP-B,DC-X,200,200,WZ-1,Insp,"1 pallet holds CMP-A (10 pcs)"\n'
    )
    graph = build(root)
    result = compute(graph.records, graph.issues)
    cards = build_cards(result, graph.issues, graph.records)
    blocked = next(c for c in cards if c.id.startswith("wrong"))
    assert blocked.blocked_only and blocked.at_risk == 0
    assert "do any packed copies already contain this stock?" in blocked.messages[0].body

"""Planning adapters, the plan-vs-paper and old-revision checks, and parse_count."""

import hashlib
import json

import openpyxl

from ask_soony.verifier.linker import build
from ask_soony.verifier.linker.normalize import parse_count
from ask_soony.verifier.linker.tests.conftest import write


def test_parse_count_reads_any_notation():
    assert parse_count("42.900") == 42900
    assert parse_count("42,900") == 42900

def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="ask_soony.verifier.impact")
    parser.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=Path("data/portal"))
    parser.add_argument("--readings", type=Path, default=Path("data/store/image_recognizer"))
    args = parser.parse_args()

    graph = build(args.root, args.readings)
    result = compute(graph.records, graph.issues)

    print("Editions")
    for e in result.editions:
        at_risk, part = result.at_risk(e.product)
        risk = f"  at risk {_n(at_risk)} (binding part {part})" if at_risk else ""
        print(
            f"  {e.product:<12} day one {_n(e.day_one):>8}  packed {_n(e.packed):>8}  "
            f"remaining {_n(e.remaining):>7}{risk}"
        )
    print("\nParts (system view → evidence view)")
    for p in result.parts:
        flag = "SHORT" if p.gap else "ok"
        counts = f"need {_n(p.needed):>7}  book {_n(p.book_stock):>8}  usable {_n(p.usable):>8}"
        used_by = ", ".join(p.editions)
        print(
            f"  {p.part:<12} {counts}  gap {_n(p.gap):>7}  {flag:<5}  "
            f"plan said: {p.plan_status or '-'}  [{used_by}]"
        )
        for d in p.deductions:
            print(f"      - {_n(d.units)} {d.reason} ({d.issue})")
        for s in p.supply:
            where = s.get("reference") or s.get("document", "")
            print(f"      + option: {s['kind']} {_n(s['quantity'] or 0)} {where}")
    for x in result.excluded:
        print(f"\n  not counted: {x['part']} for {x['edition']}: fitted inside {x['inside']}")
        print(f"    evidence: {x['evidence']}")
    if result.shared_gaps:
        print("\nShared parts short (who gets them is a decision):")
        for p in result.shared_gaps:
            print(f"  {p.part}: {_n(p.gap)} short across {', '.join(p.editions)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":

# ---- inbound that lands before packing ends (launch day here is Sun 1 Mar 2026)

ADVICE = "suppliers/SUP-0007_Acme_Parts/order_confirmations/Shipping_advice_020-1_9100000002.pdf"


def inbound_plan(root, rows):
    """A launch plan with an Inbound table (supplier, part, quantity, ..., status)."""
    wb = openpyxl.Workbook()
    ws = wb.active
    ws.title = "Inbound"
    ws.append(
        ["Supplier", "Part", "Quantity", "Mode", "Reference", "ETD", "ETA", "Status", "Comment"]
    )
    for row in rows:
        ws.append(["Acme Parts", *row, None])
    (root / "soony/context").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    wb.save(root / "soony/context/plan.xlsx")


def shipping_advice(root, readings, shipped, expected):
    """The supplier's shipping advice for AWB 020-1, read: CMP-A shipped `shipped`."""
    folder = readings / "advice"
    folder.mkdir(parents=True)
    sha = hashlib.sha256((root / ADVICE).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    (folder / "meta.json").write_text(json.dumps({"path": ADVICE, "sha256": sha, "status": "ok"}))

    def value(field, raw, number):
        return {
            "field": field,
            "field_label": None,
            "value": raw,
            "number": number,
            "unit": None,
            "written": "printed",
            "crossed_out": False,
            "legible": "clear",
        }

    (folder / "verdict.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "document_type": "shipping_advice",
                "references": [{"type": "air_waybill", "value": "020-1"}],
                "lines": [
                    {
                        "item": "1",
                        "material_id": "CMP-A",
                        "supplier_part_no": None,
                        "description": None,
                        "values": [
                            value("quantity_shipped", str(shipped), shipped),
                            value("date_expected", expected, None),
                        ],
                    }
                ],
                "statements": [],
                "corrections": [],
                "decisions": [],
                "verdict": {
                    "status": "has_warnings",
                    "summary_en": "",
                    "red_flags": [],
                    "confidence": "high",
                    "observations": [],
                },
            }
        )
    )


PLAN_ROWS = [
    ("CMP-A", 30, "air", "AWB-IN", "2026-02-27", "2026-02-28", "booked"),  # lands in time
    ("CMP-A", 1000, "sea", "CONT-LATE", "2026-02-01", "2026-03-05", "in transit"),  # after launch
    ("CMP-A", 500, "air", "AWB-X", "2026-02-27", "2026-02-28", "cancelled"),
    ("CMP-A", 40, "air", "020-1", "2026-02-27", "2026-02-28", "booked"),  # has a shipping advice
]


def test_inbound_before_packing_ends_closes_part_of_the_gap(tmp_path):
    root = portal_with_plan(tmp_path)
    inbound_plan(root, PLAN_ROWS)
    readings = tmp_path / "readings"
    failed_inspection(root, readings)  # CMP-A: 550 usable for 600 needed

    result = compute(graph.records, graph.issues)

    assert [(a["reference"], a["quantity"]) for a in part_a.arriving] == [("AWB-IN", 30)]
    assert part_a.gap == 600 - 550 - 30

Note for Farhan: change to the shortfall calculation (Sun 22 Nov, early morning)

Hi Farhan, while you were asleep we changed one calculation in impact/shortfall.py. Nothing is
committed or pushed; it is all in the working tree for you to review.

What was wrong
- PartNeed.gap was needed - usable stock. It ignored supply that is already on its way and
  lands in Hamburg before packing ends (Sun 20:00).
- Example: the game card card said 34,800 short (153,200 needed - 118,400 book stock as of
  20 Nov). Hwaseong's air freight 020-48113256 (PO 4500318735) lands on 21 Nov; its shipping
  advice says 28,000 of 48,000 were flown, the 20,000 balance lands Tue 24 Nov (after launch).
  The real gap is 6,800, which is also what papercheck.py rule a computes.

What changed
- shortfall.py: new PartNeed.arriving and PartNeed.not_counted lists, new property
  arriving_in_time, and gap = needed - usable - arriving_in_time. gap_if_acted, at_risk and
  the cards follow automatically.
- New function _arriving() fills both lists. Sources: plan_inbound rows, plus ERP shipment rows
  (newest per reference; quantity from their open PO lines when the plan has no row). It counts
  an inbound only if:
  - ETA is on or before launch day (same cut-off as the existing after_launch rule)
  - not cancelled and not "arrived" at the port (that stays a collect fix, not available stock)
  - no goods receipt for its PO and part between its ETD and the stock date (that would already
    be in the book stock); a receipt after the stock date counts with the received quantity
  - not overdue (ETA before the stock date and no receipt: treated as lost, not as supply)
  - the supplier's shipping document for the same reference does not say less; if it does,
    only the shipped quantity counts and the balance goes to not_counted with its expected date
  - if such a shipping document exists but has no reading yet, it is NOT counted (reason
    "not read yet"), because the paper may be a short-shipment advice like this one
- cards.py (allocate card only): paper_says, the decision question and the approver message use
  stock + arriving; evidence lists what was counted as arriving and what was not, and why.
- Tests: 5 new tests in impact/tests/test_shortfall.py (in-time vs after-launch vs cancelled vs
  unread advice; shipped short with balance, card disappears when the gap closes; receipt before
  and after the stock date; overdue shipment). Full suite: 219 passed, ruff clean.

Important: readings
- There is no data/store/image_recognizer on Jonas's Mac, so the shipping advice has no reading
  there. With the rule above the dispatch run there still says 34,800 short, and now names the
  unread advice under "Not counted". Once the advice is read (your readings store, or one
  image_recognizer run with --only Shipping_advice_020-48113256), the same run gives
  6,800 short.
- We checked this with a hand transcription of that one PDF as a temporary reading (outside the
  repo, not committed): 6,800 short, allocate card still there, 20,000 balance not counted.

Not changed, worth a look
- runs_dry still uses usable stock only, so the allocate card's act-by time ignores arrivals.
- impact/__main__.py does not print the arriving list yet (the gap it prints is the new one).
- The plan's due_before_launch column (48,000) is still the system view; we did not use it.

I made the fix, but on this Mac the game card gap still shows 34,800. The rule needs a reading of Hwaseong's shipping advice, and there is none locally (`data/store/image_recognizer` doesn't exist). With a reading of that one PDF the same run gives 6,800 short, exactly what the paper check computes. Nothing is committed or pushed.

**The change**
- **`shortfall.py`:** each part now carries two new lists. `arriving` holds inbound that is counted, with reference, quantity, ETA and basis. `not_counted` holds inbound that is skipped, with the reason. `gap` is now needed − usable − arriving. `gap_if_acted`, `at_risk` and the cards pick this up automatically.
- **What counts as arriving:** a launch-plan inbound row, or an ERP shipment (quantity from its open PO lines), if all of these hold:
  - ETA is on or before launch day.
  - It is not cancelled, and not "arrived" at the port (that stays a collect fix).
  - It has no goods receipt dated between its ETD and the stock date (that would already be in stock). A receipt after the stock date counts at the received quantity.
  - It is not overdue (ETA before the stock date with no receipt).
  - The supplier's shipping document doesn't say less. If it does, only the shipped quantity counts and the balance goes to `not_counted` with its expected date.
- **Unread documents:** if a shipping document exists for the reference but nobody has read it yet, the inbound is not counted. That is the conservative choice: counting the plan's 48,000 would have shown no gap at all, when the paper actually says short.
- **The Hwaseong balance:** the 20,000 arriving Tue 24 Nov is never counted.
- **`cards.py` (allocate card only):** the "what the paper says" line, the decision question and the approver message now use stock plus arriving. The evidence lists what was counted and what wasn't, and why.

**Before and after on the real data**

| Part | Before | No reading (this Mac) | With a reading of the advice |
|---|---|---|---|
| CMP-GAM-001 game card | 34,800 short | 34,800 short; the 48,000 is listed as not counted, "not read yet" | 6,800 short (118,400 stock + 28,000 arriving; 20,000 balance not counted) |
| CMP-GAM-004 | gap 0 | gap 0; Karton Nowak's 20,000 (PO 7K21M) now counted as arriving | gap 0 |
| CMP-GAM-003 | 32,000 short | unchanged; the 350,000 at the port is still a collect fix | unchanged |

- **Allocate card:** it still appears in both runs because a gap remains. With the reading its title reads "6,800 short across 2 editions". A test confirms the card disappears once the gap closes.
- **Paper check difference:** none once the advice is read. The paper check does 153,200 − (118,400 + 48,000 due − 20,000 late) = 6,800, which is the same number. Without the reading, the whole difference is the 28,000 the verifier can't confirm.

The "with a reading" run used a reading I transcribed by hand from the PDF's text into the scratch folder. It is not in the repo and is not a real reader output. The dispatch output is at `/Users/jonasstenglein/.claude/jobs/3021cc1a/tmp/verifier-fix/dispatch.json`, and the reading-based one is `dispatch_with_reading.json` next to it. Nothing was written to `data/state`.

**Tests:** I added 5 tests to `src/ask_soony/verifier/impact/tests/test_shortfall.py`. `uv run pytest -q` gives 219 passed, and `ruff check` is clean. `ruff format --check` flags two files in `dispatch/decisions` that I didn't edit; they were already like that.

**Decision for you:** to get 6,800 on the live dashboard, the advice needs a real reading. That means one paid OpenAI run of the image recognizer on that file (`--only Shipping_advice_020-48113256`), which I did not do without your OK.

**Left for Farhan** (all in his note):
- The "runs dry" time, and so the allocate card's act-by time, still uses stock on hand only and ignores arrivals.
- `impact/__main__.py` doesn't print the arriving list yet.
